answer: A glacier moves slowly, and trust should too. New identities begin in a narrow inlet where they may take only tiny paid jobs, each checked by a reviewer drawn at random, while earnings stay locked for thirty days. A reviewer who passes bad work loses a 50-credit bond, so checks stay honest. After thirty clean jobs an identity reaches the open mesa of full work, yet one failed check burns its locked balance and sends it back to the inlet. A thousand fakes must finish 30,000 real checked jobs and risk 50,000 credits in bonds before earning anything.
